metaDescription: Six weighted blankets compared on weight, size, pocket stitching, cover fabric, heat and washing, with picks for sofas, hot sleepers and cold rooms.
expertTake: The Smart Queen 20 pound blanket is our top pick because its quilted 5 inch pockets and cotton shell address the two common complaints, shifting beads and heat. The L'AGRATY 48 by 72 inch throw is the value pick for one person on a sofa. Skip a weighted blanket if you run hot, share a bed or cannot easily lift it off, because the weight is the whole point and also the whole drawback.
introParagraphs: A weighted blanket is a quilted blanket filled with small beads or pellets, so it presses gently on the body. People use them on a sofa or in bed because they enjoy the feeling of the weight, and some find it calming.

The evidence that weighted blankets help anxiety or sleep is limited, so treat any benefit as possible, not proven. What you can judge is construction: weight, size, pocket stitching, cover fabric and washing. This guide compares those and shows which designs suit a sofa throw and which suit a bed.

products.name: Smart Queen Weighted Blanket 20 lb, 60 x 80 In, Cotton

specList.label: Fill
specList.value: Glass beads in 5 x 5 inch pockets

products.description:
Smart Queen fills each 5 by 5 inch quilted pocket with glass beads and stitches the pockets tightly so the weight stays spread across the blanket. The shell is cotton, which lets air move, and the listing says it is machine washable. At 20 pounds in a 60 by 80 inch size, it is meant for a larger adult or a bed.

Bead migration is the usual failure of cheap weighted blankets, and small pockets with dense stitching are the best defense. Cotton is cooler than fleece or minky, but it is also less cozy in a cold room. A 20 pound blanket in a queen size suits a person near 200 pounds by the 10 percent guideline, and it is too heavy for many people.

A heavy cotton blanket can overload a home washer, so use a large capacity machine or a laundromat and dry it fully. Compared with the Yescool, which has the same weight and pocket size, the Smart Queen leads on the cotton shell. It suits a bed or a long sofa for a heavier adult. Lay it flat on a table once a month and smooth any bead clusters toward the center to keep the weight even.
products.bestFor: Heavier adults and hot sleepers who want a cotton shell and tight pockets.
pros: Quilted 5 inch pockets keep the glass beads spread evenly
Cotton shell breathes better than fleece or minky
20 pounds suits a heavier adult by the 10 percent guideline
Machine washable, though a large washer is needed
cons: 20 pounds is too heavy for many adults and children
Cotton feels cooler in a cold room than fleece

products.name: L'AGRATY Weighted Blanket 15 lb, 48 x 72 In, Dark Grey
products.description:
L'AGRATY makes a 15 pound throw in a 48 by 72 inch size, with a breathable microfiber shell and fine glass beads of 0.8 to 1 millimeter. The listing recommends 7 to 12 percent of body weight, which puts it at the right weight for a person of about 125 to 215 pounds. It is the cheapest blanket in this lineup.

The smaller size is the strength: it covers one person on a sofa or a twin bed without hanging over the sides, and a smaller area feels heavier. Microfiber is soft but warmer than cotton, and it can pill with washing. The listing describes a positioning technology to keep beads in place, which is a claim we could not verify.

Wash gently and air dry if you can. Compared with the Smart Queen, the L'AGRATY is lighter and smaller, so it suits a sofa. It suits a single person and a living room. If you later decide you like the feel, you can step up to a heavier queen without wasting the throw, which keeps working on a sofa.
products.bestFor: One person on a sofa or twin bed who wants a lighter throw.
pros: 48 by 72 inch size fits one person without overhang
Fine glass beads of 0.8 to 1 millimeter feel smooth
Weight guideline of 7 to 12 percent is stated clearly
Lowest in the price order of this lineup
cons: Microfiber runs warmer than cotton and can pill
Bead positioning claim could not be verified

products.name: Mr. Sandman Cooling Weighted Blanket 15 lb, Queen
products.description:
Mr. Sandman's cooling blanket is a 15 pound queen with a soft minky fabric that is reversible, designed for use all year. The surface carries an embossed pattern, which makes it look like a decor blanket on a bed.

Minky is a polyester fabric that feels soft but traps heat, so the cooling name is a marketing label rather than a measured property. For a hot sleeper a cotton shell is a more dependable choice. Compared with the Smart Queen, the Mr. Sandman is lighter at 15 pounds and richer in feel. Because it is queen size, it can hang over a sofa edge.

Wash gently and avoid high heat, since polyester flattens. It suits a bed where the look matters as much as the weight.
products.bestFor: Bed use where a soft, reversible, decorative finish matters.
pros: Reversible minky surface gives two looks in one blanket
Embossed pattern reads as decor on a bed
15 pounds suits many adults by the 10 percent guideline
Queen size covers a bed for one or two
cons: Cooling is a marketing label and minky traps heat
Queen size overhangs a sofa seat awkwardly

products.name: Yescool Weighted Blanket 20 lb, 60 x 80 In, Grey
products.description:
Yescool sells a 20 pound queen blanket in grey with 5 by 5 inch compartments and a recommendation of about 10 percent of body weight. The listing positions it for single use in a queen size, which gives a generous drape.

The compartments are the same size as the Smart Queen, so bead shifting is limited, but the shell is a polyester blend with a cooling label. A 20 pound blanket in a queen is heavy to lift and heavy to wash. The 60 by 80 inch size covers a bed but overhangs a sofa seat. Yescool also makes a king size at the same weight, which feels lighter per area.

Check the care label before washing, since a heavy blanket can overload a machine. It suits a bed where one adult wants a heavy cover. A thick duvet cover over it, if the blanket has loops, protects the shell and makes laundry easier.
products.bestFor: Single adults in a queen bed who want a heavy blanket.
pros: 20 pounds gives a heavy, even feel for larger adults
5 by 5 inch compartments limit bead shifting
Grey color blends with most bedding
Stated 10 percent body weight guideline helps choose
cons: Heavy to lift, wash and move for many people
Cooling label does not mean the shell is cotton cool

products.name: Cottonblue Sherpa Weighted Blanket 15 lb, Queen 60 x 80
products.description:
Cottonblue's 15 pound queen uses fleece and sherpa at 220 GSM, which is a soft, warm surface for cold rooms. The listing says the fabric resists fading and stains. It is a blanket for winter, a sofa during movies, or a cold bedroom.

Sherpa is warm, which makes weighted plus sherpa too hot for many in summer. Fleece and sherpa also shed fibers, collect pet hair and mat if washed hot. Compared with the Mr. Sandman, which is smoother, this one is fluffier and warmer. Queen size is large, so on a sofa it will drape over the floor.

Wash cold and tumble on low, or air dry. It suits someone who gets cold easily. Keep it away from a lint roller habit by brushing it with a soft brush after the first few washes, since new sherpa sheds the most early on.
products.bestFor: Cold rooms and winter sofas where warmth matters most.
pros: 220 GSM fleece and sherpa gives a very soft, warm feel
15 pounds suits many adults by the 10 percent guideline
Fade and stain resistance is stated in the listing
Fluffy texture works as a decor blanket on a sofa
cons: Sherpa is too warm for summer or for hot sleepers
Sherpa sheds and collects pet hair

products.name: Wemore Sherpa Weighted Blanket 15 lb, Twin 48 x 72 In
products.description:
Wemore makes a 15 pound twin throw, 48 by 72 inches, with a 220 GSM fleece top and a 220 GSM sherpa underside, and glass beads in a seven layer design. The two textures mean you can pick a smooth or a fluffy side.

The small size makes it the sofa pick among the sherpa blankets, and it fits a twin bed as well. Sherpa and fleece are warm, so it suits cold rooms more than summer. Compared with the Cottonblue queen, the Wemore twin is more manageable and less likely to drag on the floor. Shedding in the first washes is common with sherpa.

Wash inside out on cold and dry on low. It suits a single person on a sofa in a cool room. Use the fleece side when you want less shedding on clothes and the sherpa side when you want extra warmth.
products.bestFor: Single sofa use in a cool room with a soft sherpa side.
pros: Dual sided fleece and sherpa gives two textures
48 by 72 inch size fits a sofa or a twin bed
Glass beads in a seven layer design stay spread
15 pounds suits many adults near 150 pounds
cons: Sherpa and fleece run warm, which hot sleepers will dislike
Sherpa sheds fibers in the first few washes

buyingCriteria.explanation: The common guideline is about 7 to 12 percent of your body weight, with listings quoting 7 to 12, 8 to 12 or 10 percent. A 15 pound blanket suits a person of about 125 to 215 pounds, and a 20 pound one suits a person near 200 pounds. It is a guideline, not a rule, so lean lighter if unsure. Weigh yourself, multiply by 0.10, and round to the nearest available blanket weight, then decide whether to go one step lighter.

A 48 by 72 inch throw like the L'AGRATY suits one person on a sofa or a twin bed, while 60 by 80 inches suits a queen bed. The same weight in a smaller area feels heavier. Buy by how you will use it, not by the bed size. If you move the blanket between rooms, the smaller size is also much easier to carry.

Small pockets, like the 5 by 5 inch ones on the Smart Queen and Yescool, keep beads from pooling at the edges. Wide pockets let beads shift. Glass beads are finer and quieter than plastic pellets. Open the seam on a spare corner of an old blanket if you want to see how loose or tight the fill is, which tells you more than a listing does.

Cotton on the Smart Queen breathes best, while fleece, sherpa and minky on the Cottonblue, Wemore and Mr. Sandman run warm. A cooling label does not make polyester cool. Hot sleepers should choose cotton. If you wake sweaty, switch to a lighter weight before changing anything else.

A heavy blanket can overload a home washer, and wet glass beads add weight. Check the care label, use a large machine and dry fully to avoid mildew. A removable cover is easier to care for. A laundromat machine with a large drum handles a wet queen blanket far better than a standard home unit.

Weighted blankets are not for infants or toddlers, and anyone with breathing or circulation issues should ask a clinician. You must be able to remove it yourself. Evidence for benefits is limited, so treat them as a comfort item. Read the manufacturer's own safety notes before the first night. Keep pets off the blanket when you are not under it so a small animal never gets trapped beneath the weight.

howWeEvaluated.title: Weight and size
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared weights, sizes and the stated guideline. The L'AGRATY at 48 by 72 inches and the Yescool at 60 by 80 inches set the range. We noted the use each size suits.

howWeEvaluated.title: Construction
howWeEvaluated.description: We read the pocket size and fill notes. The 5 by 5 inch pockets on the Smart Queen and Yescool scored best. These are editorial assessments based on the spec sheet.

howWeEvaluated.title: Fabric and heat
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared cotton, microfiber, minky and sherpa. Cotton scored best for heat. We noted that cooling labels are marketing claims.

howWeEvaluated.title: Washing and care
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at machine washability and size of the blanket. Heavy blankets strain home washers. We noted the benefit of covers.

howWeEvaluated.title: Ownership patterns
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at owner feedback patterns about bead leaks, heat and shedding. These shaped the cons. We make no medical claims.

maintenance.why: Some weighted blankets need a gentle cycle or a laundromat. Heavy loads strain a home washer.
Wet beads cause mildew if not dried. Use low heat or air dry.
Spot cleaning reduces full washes, which age the stitching.
Stray beads mean a seam is opening. Repair early or stop using the blanket.
Beads can drift to one side over time. Shake the blanket flat to spread them.

faq.q: How heavy should a weighted blanket be?
faq.a: A common guideline is 7 to 12 percent of body weight, with about 10 percent a typical target. If unsure, choose the lighter one.
Fleece, sherpa and minky run warm. Cotton shells like the Smart Queen breathe better.

faq.q: Can I wash it at home?
faq.a: Many can be machine washed but heavy ones can overload a home washer. Check the label and use a large machine.

faq.q: Do weighted blankets help anxiety or sleep?
faq.a: The evidence is limited and mixed, so treat benefits as possible. They are a comfort item, not a treatment.
Not for infants or toddlers. Ask a pediatrician before using one for a child.
Choose a throw for a sofa and one person, and a queen for a bed. A smaller blanket at the same weight feels heavier.
